ranked.headline: Foundation models recover molecular cell state from histology, spatial and multi-omic data
ranked.summary: New preprints push H&E images and spatial spots toward single-cell molecular readouts while large pretrained models reshape cell and gene representations.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of single-cell molecular state from tissue and cell measurements. Three preprints treat H&E as a molecular readout. Loki2, trained on 15 million cells, tests how much molecular and cellular state routine histology encodes. GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes and maps senescence across aging mouse organs and human skin. sc-HistoMorphomics links 194 nuclear morphometric features to spatial transcriptomics. Spatial methods also move toward cellular resolution. st2sc infers single-cell expression from multicellular spots, a rotation-equivariant network learns 3D subcellular transcript embeddings, and CIRCA recovers identifiable cell and niche programs linked to pathology. Representation learning continues to scale. Bloom unifies expression and chromatin accessibility across 300,000 mouse brain cells, MCT models cell sets to learn gene co-regulation, and scUNVEIL pretrains on about 92 million human cells. Other work targets dynamics and inference: GFM for unseen Perturb-seq responses, DRAFT for dynamic GRNs, CIRCE for graded signaling, and GatorAnchor for neighborhood uncertainty.

ranked.headline: Protein language models are being adapted with task-specific signals for function prediction
ranked.summary: New preprints pair protein language model embeddings with dynamics, structure, reaction or geometric inputs to predict variant effects, kcat, PTMs and more.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the specialization of protein sequence representations for defined prediction tasks through added task-relevant information, rather than reliance on generic embeddings. DynamicsPLM adds molecular dynamics heads to a 35M-parameter model to predict zero-shot variant effects. HieraPTM combines sequence, language model and 3D structure features to move from PTM site recognition to functional phosphosite prediction. EnzRef models reactants and products separately against a frozen model, using reference-centered adaptation for kcat. SMSTPred and PhageLysClass apply embeddings to methyltransferase substrate specificity and phage lytic protein classes. CarmnaDD predicts nitrogenase activity from sequence with dual descriptors (R2 0.60, AUC 0.94). A methodological counterpoint: one benchmark finds that embedding anisotropy degrades remote-homology retrieval relative to MMseqs2 and Foldseek, and that ZCA whitening addresses it. Other items, including FoldMapper, MANTA, AbPoolRank and MicroDUET, address inverse folding, disordered ensembles, antibody–antigen complex ranking and genomic surveillance.

ranked.headline: Automation and registration push neural cell profiling toward tissue-scale multimodal maps
ranked.summary: New preprints automate Patch-seq, atlas-based neuron identification, glomerulus mapping and cross-modality image registration for single-cell spatial analysis.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is scaling quantitative cell characterization by coupling automation with multimodal registration. Patch-seq work shows that detergent-cleaned reusable pipettes, robotic nucleus extraction and sonication preserve electrophysiology and transcriptomic yield. In C. elegans, probabilistic atlases from near-wild-type strains reach 86.3% top-1 variability-aware neuron identification. Whole-bulb light-sheet expansion microscopy with automated segmentation quantifies thousands of glomeruli in intact mouse olfactory bulbs. SCOUBI infers axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic transcripts in spatial transcriptomics. A parallel strand integrates imaging modalities: MeXalign coregisters LA-ICP-TOFMS and immunofluorescence via segmentation masks, and FluoMALDI links fluorescence-defined genes, proteins and organelles to spatial lipid composition. Disease- and glia-focused tools add 3D readouts: PASTA resolves amyloid-beta plaque heterogeneity and microglial contacts, and PolyMorph3D quantifies microglia morphology with multi-marker colocalization. Stitched montage cryo-ET of lamellipodial actin is methodologically related but lies outside neural tissue.

ranked.headline: CRISPRi knockdown responses shift across cell lines and aging cohorts
ranked.summary: Two CRISPRi preprints show knockdown responses and rejuvenation rankings depend on cell line and cohort, limiting naive transfer of perturbation results.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how far CRISPRi perturbation responses generalize beyond the context in which they were measured. CRISPRi Perturb-seq of essential genes in four human cell lines finds a median cross-line response correlation of 0.52. Transfer to a new line requires screening about 30% of it. A separate analysis of CRISPRi screens ranked for reversal of aging expression signatures finds that the rankings change with the aging cohort used and track proliferation programs, pointing to growth-related confounding. The previously noted comparison of drug-perturbation resources is not among the current items, so that claim is dropped. Adjacent methods address technical confounding and prediction rather than CRISPRi itself. These include cross-modal anchored batch correction for TCGA multi-omics, DeepRNAi for siRNA on- and off-target prediction, ARC-Impute and spicyR v2 for spatial omics, and assay-level comparisons covering Siphon-seq platelet profiling, Catch*ReSeq isoform enrichment and cell-free RNA extraction platforms.

ranked.headline: ROS and redox modules couple stress signaling to hormones, lipids and fruit development
ranked.summary: New preprints and Plant Physiology papers map specific redox regulators, from 2-Cys peroxiredoxins to ZAT11/12, onto defined stress and fruit traits.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is ROS and redox state acting through defined protein modules rather than as generic damage. In Arabidopsis, peroxisomal H2O2 homeostasis under PEG-induced water stress rebalances ABA and GA metabolism to slow seed germination. 2-Cys peroxiredoxins interact with FAD7/FAD8 to raise phosphatidylglycerol trienoic fatty acids and support PSII recovery after high light. H2S-dependent persulfidation and PRMT5-dependent LSm4 methylation link H2S signaling to alternative splicing in stomatal closure. In fruit trees, MxMPK4-1 phosphorylates NADP-malic enzyme MxME3-7 at S201 to enhance ROS-mediated iron-deficiency tolerance in apple. In pear, a PUB8–ZAT11/12–LAC1 module drives ROS-linked lignin polymerization and stone cell formation. Related work covers ursolic acid control of ascorbate via MdGGP2 and MdAPX1 in fresh-cut apple, and melatonin plus selenium nanoparticles in salt-stressed soybean acting via MAPK signaling and lipid remodeling. A superoxide dismutase review provides historical and evolutionary context.

ranked.headline: Germline and gametogenic gene regulation depends on piRNA, stress, and RNA-processing factors
ranked.summary: New preprints link COPS5, meiotic stress pathways, HLH-30/TFEB and rRNA-dependent histone processing to germline function, alongside Drosophila RNA-binding and snoRNP studies.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how specific regulators sustain gene expression programs and genome integrity in germline and gametogenic contexts. In mouse germ cells, COPS5 loss downregulates piRNA pathway genes, lowers pachytene piRNAs, derepresses LINE1 and IAP, and arrests spermatogenesis. In budding yeast meiosis, Hsf1, Skn7, Msn2 and Msn4 are active without external stress, and TSA1 and AHP1 protect gametes. In C. elegans, HLH-30/TFEB loss alters the basal transcriptome and reduces sperm and progeny numbers, while disrupted rRNA biogenesis causes histone mRNA 3' misprocessing. Drosophila work adds Marf1 integration into accessory gland regulation and GAR1-linked H/ACA snoRNP control of sgg splicing and insulin signaling. Ovarian aging and mitochondrial-nuclear yeast screens extend the scope beyond germline silencing.

ranked.headline: Repeated sampling of living tissue and richer per-cell readouts extend spatial transcriptomics
ranked.summary: LIFE-seq and LANCE-seq enable repeated spatial sampling of living tissue, while FULL-seq and SpaceMACE add isoform and spatial context to expression data.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is extending spatial and single-cell transcriptomics beyond static, single-timepoint measurement. LIFE-seq (nanoforest arrays) and LANCE-seq (encoded microneedle arrays) sample living tissue repeatedly; LIFE-seq follows cortical injury in the same mouse, and LANCE-seq profiles mouse brain and tracks APAP-induced liver injury over time. FULL-seq joins chromatin accessibility with full-length transcripts per cell, linking promoter regulation to alternative first exon usage. SpaceMACE adds spatial proximity and expression similarity to tumour-cell annotation. PDAC BioPortal integrates bulk, single-nucleus and spatial cohorts. The remaining items apply transcriptomic profiling to cervical tissue and cancer or to KDM3B-driven ErbB signaling in cholangiocarcinoma, and they do not share the methodological emphasis on temporal or spatial resolution.

ranked.headline: Rapid adaptation under strong selection rests on haploblocks, polygenic parallelism and plasticity
ranked.summary: New preprints link genomic architecture of rapid adaptation to population persistence, extinction and climate-response prediction across insects, fish and plants.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how the genetic architecture of adaptation determines persistence under abrupt or sustained environmental change. In cowpea seed beetles, rapid, repeatable rescue on lentil relies on large non-recombining haploblocks on chromosomes 1 and 9. In outdoor Drosophila under insecticide stress, half of populations went extinct despite strong parallel polygenic adaptation, with pre-adaptation implicated in preventing extinction. Related work addresses selection through time and across environments: seasonal adaptive tracking in Drosophila suzukii, pooled-sequencing of chronotype selection lines, and gradient-based GWAS in Boechera stricta suggesting projected hot, dry climates may exceed adaptive capacity. Stickleback studies separate within- and transgenerational plasticity architectures and show sex-specific responses to paternal predation cues. What is new is the joint treatment of haplotype structure, contingency, and plasticity in outcomes of rescue.

ranked.headline: Microbiome studies link resolved genomes and diversity metrics to ecological structure and function
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair long-read and genome-resolved metagenomics with new diversity frameworks to resolve community structure across biofilm, sediment, sludge and host systems.
ranked.synthesis: The items converge on resolving microbial community structure and function across habitats, from marble biofilms, river biofilms and reef sediments to activated sludge, oral biofilms and octocoral hosts. Methodological advances stand out: HiFi long-read metagenomics recovers denitrifiers, nitrifiers and Accumulibacter missed by short-read assemblies, while genome-resolved sediment work yields 2,698 mostly novel MAGs. hilldiv3 unifies neutral, phylogenetic and functional Hill-number analysis, and MiSA provides statistical detection of spatial dysbiosis in image-based oral data. Ecological findings contrast turnover with conservation: marble biofilms show taxonomic turnover with conserved phylogenetic structure, octocoral microbiomes remain host-specific and temporally stable over three years, and river microeukaryotes track water chemistry as condition indicators. The items are heterogeneous in system and method, but share an emphasis on higher-resolution inference.

ranked.headline: Locus-specific histone methylation, its erasure, and protection define where repressive chromatin is installed
ranked.summary: New preprints and papers resolve how H3K4, H3K9 and H3K27 methylation are targeted, erased or shielded to control silencing and cell identity.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how silencing is gated at specific loci by the writers, erasers, recruiters and chaperones acting on histone methylation. H3K4 methylation and DNA methylation cooperatively shield regulatory elements from Polycomb in mouse ES cells, while in Arabidopsis Pol II Ser2P redistribution into gene bodies recruits the FLD-LD H3K4me1 demethylase complex to license silencing. PRC2/H3K27me3 is targeted by maternal Foxh1 in Xenopus, shapes PHE1 behavior at imprinted genes in endosperm, and depends on CAF-1 in Neurospora. H3K9 pathways include SETDB1 recruitment by IDC, STWL and PZG at phf7 in Drosophila, and EHMT1/2 acting through H3K9me2-dependent and -independent mechanisms in cortical neurogenesis. The new elements are mechanistic: recruitment, protection and erasure steps that determine developmental timing and identity.

ranked.headline: Cell-type and stage-resolved omics expose early synaptic, proteostatic and transcriptional defects in neural disease
ranked.summary: New preprints apply cell-type, temporal and variant-level profiling to map early molecular changes in Huntington, ALS, Fmr1-KO and GBA1 disease models.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving disease-associated molecular change by cell type, age or stage. In R6/1 mice, proteomics shows synaptic protein loss in excitatory neurons and reduced glial neuronal-support proteins before motor onset, while aged TgHD minipig putamen shows age-dependent transcript and protein changes, including reduced D2 neuron markers. Fmr1-KO profiling reveals cell type-specific remodelling of excitatory and inhibitory synapses. In ALS-related work, a TDP-43 APEX2 atlas finds interactome changes persisting after stress recovery, somatic mutation burden is higher in younger ALS donors with an SBS5 signature, and SETX loss shows stage-dependent effects in iPSC motor neurons. A multiplexed assay maps GBA1 variant activity, and Ankle2-VRK1 work links proteostasis to neuronal resilience in aging Drosophila. Not all items address aging.

ranked.headline: Omics readouts shift with evaluation depth, scoring method, cell composition and compartment
ranked.summary: Eight preprints show that depth, scoring and compartment determine which omics conclusions hold, favoring explicit reporting of these conditions.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that quantitative omics inferences depend on how and where they are evaluated. Proteomic co-abundance method rankings change with evaluation depth, and colorectal stress granule contrasts between fibroblasts and epithelium depend on scoring method and depth. Post-stroke efferocytosis transcript readouts are bounded by cell composition and time rather than flux, and replicate libraries set a noise floor for cell-state claims in drug-tolerant PC9 cells. Compartment specificity recurs in the cochlea, where ageing shows weak systemic concordance and macrophages follow a distinct programme, and in cortical GABAergic neurons, where channel expression aligns with dendritic conductance load in a reinforcing direction. Further, cell-state conditioning predicts responses to an unseen stimulus but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects. The new element is the emphasis on explicit depth, scoring and replicate-aware controls.

ranked.headline: Sequence models and eQTL frameworks map regulatory variant effects to cell types, tissues and ancestry
ranked.summary: Eight preprints link predicted and observed regulatory variant effects to cell states, tissues and ancestry, from AlphaGenome 2 to T2D effector-gene prioritization.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is placing regulatory variant effects in specific cellular, tissue and genetic contexts. AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-specific regulatory activity and variant effects from 1-Mb sequence, and ChromBPNet models of 17 hematopoietic types score 302,830 variants with lineage-structured accessibility effects. Admixed whole-blood RNA-seq links West African ancestry to more allele-specific expression, with 52 ancestry-associated loci replicating. Downstream, CAS-X integrates fine-mapped eQTLs across five metabolic tissues and CELL-X uses islet single-cell transcriptomes for type 2 diabetes. PrediXSKAT weights coding variants by predicted cis-regulated expression. The endometriosis study shows cell-state prioritization depends on marker definition and donor structure. The midkine Mendelian randomization study in pancreatic cancer is only loosely related.

ranked.headline: Cell-type-resolved transcriptomic and miRNA maps refine Alzheimer mechanisms and mouse model use
ranked.summary: New preprints pair 5xFAD snRNA-seq, harmonized mouse transcriptomes and large cortical miRNA data to resolve cell-type mechanisms in Alzheimer's disease.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is cell-type-resolved omics applied to Alzheimer's disease and its models. In 5xFAD mouse brain, snRNA-seq identifies VIP interneurons as most disrupted in synapse programs and preferentially rescued by rolipram, implicating a Pde7b/CREB1 cAMP axis. A harmonized set of 1,863 mouse cortex and hippocampus samples, including AD models, enables uniform cross-study comparison. A separate study links early lysosomal biogenesis (MiT/TFE) to disease-associated microglia reprogramming across murine injury, amyloidosis and human AD. In humans, a meta-analysis of 1,738 postmortem cortices connects miRNAs, notably miR-132-3p, to tau pathology and cell-type programs. Developmental regulatory maps from 231 prefrontal cortices and VEGABrain extend this toward developmental context. The preeclampsia miRNA-mRNA study is peripheral to this thread.

ranked.headline: Single-cell and single-molecule assays resolve somatic genomic and epigenomic variation
ranked.summary: Seven preprints apply single-cell, long-read and k-mer methods to variation in retrotransposition, satellites, methylation, chromatin and karyotype.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving genomic and epigenomic variability that bulk or assembly-based measurements obscure. LUSTRE maps L1 insertions in ~17,600 adult human neurons to estimate somatic retrotransposition rates, and k-mer tools size Yq12 satellite arrays across 1,597 males, including father-son dynamics and testis-expressed satellite RNA. Methodological items extend this to the epigenome: ChIMe-seq jointly profiles histone modifications, DNA methylation and nucleosome positioning in single molecules and cells; TrES-seq pairs scRNA-seq with nanobody-based histone mark profiling in human tonsil cells; COMET assigns bulk long-read reads to cell types by methylation, separating composition shifts from within-cell changes. Two studies characterize variability directly: genome folding differs between pluripotent and hepatocyte-like cells, and acral melanomas show continuous karyotypic and structural fluctuation linked to MMBIR repair. The systems are heterogeneous, so the shared element is the measurement strategy rather than a common biological mechanism.

ranked.headline: Long-read assemblies, pangenomes and coalescent models resolve gene copy number variation
ranked.summary: Long-read genomes, a C. elegans pangenome and a count-based duplication model advance resolution and inference of gene copy number variation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is gene copy number variation, addressed through sequence-resolved genomes and model-based inference. PacBio HiFi sequencing yields near-complete de novo genomes of recently isolated Malian P. falciparum, revealing variation in telomere-associated architecture. A gene-based pangenome of 140 C. elegans strains shows that hyper-divergent regions are enriched for copy-number variable environmental response genes and identifies a novel anthelmintic resistance locus. A coalescent duplication network model infers copy number history from copy counts alone, applied to NB-ARC domain counts of NLR genes. OrthoSimulator, which generates empirically calibrated simulations with known orthology ground truth, supports benchmarking of orthology inference, a step relevant to gene family analysis. The phylogeny-localization and ancient DNA relatedness preprints are methodologically distinct and do not address copy number directly.

ranked.headline: Regulatory modules tune xylem, root and leaf anatomy to water transport and stress tolerance in grasses
ranked.summary: New grass studies link xylem and root vascular patterning and wall-gene modules to water relations and stress tolerance, from protoxylem to nodal roots.
ranked.synthesis: The items converge on regulatory modules that set tissue anatomy, particularly xylem and secondary cell wall features, and thereby physiological performance in grasses. A xylem single-cell atlas identifies ZHD3 and ZHD4 as central regulators of protoxylem morphology. In wheat, nodal root anatomy varies with culm position beyond area scaling, with distinct genetic associations after allometric correction, and metaxylem number is remodelled along root axes, with hydraulic modelling linking vessel patterning to water transport. In rice, OsWOX11 promotes thick AR2 roots, with a promoter variant (Hap3) of higher activity, and a KNOX-BELL (RLC3) module activates lignin genes to control leaf rolling and drought tolerance. In creeping bentgrass, dosage-sensitive miR164-NAC tuning separates growth, drought and salt responses via AsNHX1. Quantitative regulatory variation emerges as the common lever.

ranked.headline: Elicitor perception and immune signaling across peptide, effector, viral and metabolite triggers
ranked.summary: New reports link systemin receptor variation, fungal and viral elicitors, and N-hydroxypipecolic acid to immune activation in Nicotiana, rice, wheat and Arabidopsis.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how plants detect diverse elicitors and convert them into immune outputs. In Nicotiana, four new bioactive systemins are detected by SlSYR1, and a premature stop codon in SYR1 orthologs of LAB N. benthamiana is associated with lineage-specific insensitivity. The Ustilaginoidea virens secreted protein UvWSC1 elicits OsCPK13- and SOBIR1-dependent cell death, while SCMV HC-Pro triggers ADR1/NRG1-dependent hypersensitive death modulated by P3N-PIPO interaction. N-hydroxypipecolic acid is reported to induce systemic acquired resistance against leaf rust in wheat. In Arabidopsis, UGT74F1 and UGT74F2 restrict turnip mosaic virus independently of salicylic acid, jasmonate and RNA silencing. The mild SCMV vector for maize is a methodological tool and sits outside this thread.

ranked.headline: 22q11.2 deletion models show glial, mitophagic and barrier deficits tied to schizophrenia risk
ranked.summary: Preprints link 22q11.2 deletion phenotypes to oligodendrocyte myelination, reversible neuronal mitophagy defects and blood-brain barrier insufficiency tied to penetrance.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is cellular mechanisms underlying variable schizophrenia penetrance and neurodevelopmental phenotypes in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome. In a deletion mouse model, prefrontal cortex at P28 shows increased immature and mature oligodendrocytes with reduced myelination. In iPSC-derived neurons from deletion carriers, schizophrenia is associated with impaired mitophagy and lysosomal acidity, and restoring acidity is reported to reverse the defect. iPSC-derived blood-brain barrier cells show metabolic and structural differences linked to penetrance. What is new is the comparison of carriers with and without schizophrenia, which points to modifiable cellular states. A cntnap2-/- autism model supports oligodendroglial dysfunction causing PV interneuron hypomyelination, but it is a separate context. Cerebellar items are unrelated to 22q11.2 deletion.

ranked.headline: Reconstruction and search methods are being reworked to curb error propagation across sequence analysis
ranked.summary: Six preprints revise assembly, alignment and homology-search steps to reduce error propagation, from raw nanopore signals to GPU covariance-model search.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is rethinking a stage of sequence reconstruction or search that normally passes errors downstream. WALRUS in HyPhy 3 estimates codon alignment, phylogeny and selection tests jointly, reducing indel-driven false positives in simulated and avian data. HARICOT assembles raw nanopore signals without basecalling, using fuzzy de Bruijn graphs and Hough-transform overlap detection, and improves contiguity over the comparators. TERRACE 2.0 combines outward paired-end and chimeric reads to assemble circular RNAs from short-read RNA-seq. Infernal-GPU parallelizes covariance-model scoring, recalibrates Rfam E-values and recovers remote structured RNA homologs missed by sequence filters. Two benchmarks address upstream choices: local assembly consensus strategies for long-read structural variant calling depend on read type and error profile, and polymerase choice affects HiFi assembly contiguity and completeness.

ranked.headline: Disease and protein networks extend genetic support for therapeutic targets
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show that network propagation, tissue context and training-data domain materially change genetic target and disease inferences.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference whose outcomes depend on how biological context and network structure are encoded. BRIDGE propagates genetic evidence through protein interaction and disease-similarity networks, expanding genetic support for target-indication pairs. DEFA and SigMatch show that GWAS effector gene prioritisation performance and inferred transcriptomic disease relationships depend on training-data domain and sample tissue. Inverse Node Frequency addresses hub bias in knowledge graph metapath features for target-adverse event prediction. Separately, SNOWS integrates mutational networks with clinical data for glioma stratification, raising the C-index from 0.691 to 0.712 in an independent cohort, and a benchmark of 3D facial scan deep learning models covers screening and differential diagnosis across 18,785 subjects with rare craniofacial syndromes. What is new is the explicit quantification of how context and normalisation alter results.

ranked.headline: Glial and inflammatory programs shaping spinal cord injury repair and aging
ranked.summary: Single-cell, spatial and perturbation studies now map glial and inflammatory responses after spinal cord injury and during aging.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is glial and immune cell state in the spinal cord and related sensory tissue. Two rat studies address injury directly: a single-nucleus and spatial atlas of photoactivated cAMP-driven repair, and a comparison of contusion and bilateral dorsal hemisection models tracking neuroinflammation dynamics. A spatially resolved multi-omic atlas links aging and senescence markers to specific cell types in mouse and human spinal cord. Microglial regulation is examined in an isogenic stem cell model, where NGLY1 deficiency raises RUNX1 and alters development, phagocytosis and cytokine expression, and with an arrayed Perturb-seq platform. A pelvic pain study profiles sensory satellite glia, reporting sex-specific translatomes with mitochondrial and vesicular gene changes. The novelty lies in applying cell-type resolved, spatial and perturbational methods across injury, aging and glial contexts.

ranked.headline: Reproducibility and noise modelling challenge omics-based drug-response prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test reproducibility, noise handling and cross-modality validation in omics-based drug-response and diagnostic models.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is reproducibility and noise-aware validation in quantitative omics and drug-response modelling. A cross-resource comparison of drug-perturbation transcriptomes finds high agreement for treated expression but limited concordance of drug-induced responses across sources. A glioblastoma study shows that generative augmentation of a 38-patient circulating miRNA cohort fails to generalize across plasma and tissue cohorts, indicating that same-modality validation overstates performance. Other preprints address method-level noise: Elflow automates quality control and self-supervised representation learning for flow and mass cytometry, DeepCINET models viability assay noise in cancer cell line drug-response ranking, and BI-SCUDO Regression reports outperforming LASSO, Random Forest and XGBoost on noisy TCGA omics for survival prediction. PTM-BDL extends drug-response prediction to site-resolved phosphorylation features. The shared novelty lies in explicit noise and cross-dataset testing rather than in single-cohort accuracy.

ranked.headline: Stromal cell states and matrix programmes govern human tissue remodelling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints resolve stromal cell states and matrix-remodelling programmes across human heart, synovium, bone and fibrosis datasets.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread in these preprints is the organisation of stromal cell states and their matrix-remodelling programmes. In human atrial fibrillation, single-nucleus multi-omics resolves fibroblast and cardiomyocyte states, and JMJD1C is reported to drive TGF-beta fibroblast remodelling. Paired multiomic profiling of healthy synovium and infrapatellar fat pad describes a continuous stromal landscape. A cross-organ analysis of human and mouse fibrosis RNA-seq data identifies a conserved 25-gene matrix-remodelling core, although gene-level cross-species concordance is weak. HIPPO signalling competency links human stromal clones to bone-forming potential and osteogenic responsiveness. The full-length isoform atlas of non-failing and failing human heart and the bovine MSC transcriptomics for cultivated meat address adjacent questions of isoform diversity and culture-dependent adaptation. What is new is the resolution of stromal state continuity and fibroblast-driven matrix control at single-cell and cross-species scale.

ranked.headline: Senescent cells map to spatial niches and cell-type-specific programs in aging tissues
ranked.summary: Recent preprints resolve senescence by cell type and tissue position in aging liver and visceral adipose, with perturbation-linked evidence.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is senescence in aging tissues resolved at cell-type and spatial scale. In human omental visceral adipose, older adults show more senescent cells than obesity alone explains, with senescent stem/progenitor and mesothelial cells participating in multicellular signaling that drives inflammation. Liver studies extend this: senescent SenSpots localize to portal tracts and fibrotic septa in human metabolic liver disease, and senescent cells cluster in spatial inflammatory niches with distinct epigenetic senotypes in aged mouse liver. In aged mouse liver, p53 loss increases inflammation and metabolic damage, and MDM2 inhibitor-mediated p53 activation is reported to reverse age-linked changes. The chronic pancreatitis preprint, which concerns CD73 in metaplastic epithelium, is a related but distinct context. What is new is the combination of cell-type resolution, spatial context, and perturbation-linked evidence.

ranked.headline: ABA, JA and heat-sugar pathways tune plant stress and senescence responses
ranked.summary: Recent November 2026 papers define transcriptional and post-transcriptional controls of ABA and JA pathways in plant stress and senescence.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is transcriptional and post-transcriptional control of hormone pathways. Several items target ABA: GhNAC029 represses GhNCED1 to reduce ABA synthesis and drought tolerance in cotton; methylation of the BraCYP707A3.A02 promoter blocks BraBPC2.A08 binding, linking ABA catabolism to clubroot resistance in Brassica; and SRPKII-mediated splicing of HAB1 shapes ABA sensitivity during Arabidopsis seedling establishment. ANAC030 promotes leaf senescence by coupling JA biosynthesis to programmed cell death and chlorophyll metabolism. The miR159a-BrMYB12 module adds a myo-inositol and raffinose axis to heat tolerance in flowering Chinese cabbage. The H2A.Z study in maize addresses chromatin distribution across leaf and endosperm rather than hormone signaling. What is new is the explicit mapping of hormone-regulatory nodes to specific promoters, splice events and microRNA targets.

ranked.headline: Genotype and environment shape regulation, ionomes, and allele expression in crops
ranked.summary: Recent preprints on switchgrass, pearl millet, potato, apple, and Capsicum tie gene expression and traits to genetic background, environment, and reference choice.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that measured phenotypes and transcripts depend on genetic background, environment, and the reference framework used to interpret them. In switchgrass, field sampling across Michigan and Texas maps eQTL and GxE effects on gene regulation, selection, and leaf phosphorus traits. Pearl millet lines under drought in Senegal link foliar ionomic stability to flowering and biomass. Long-read transcriptomics of heat-stressed tetraploid potato resolves haplotype-specific expression and a heat-inducible allele. A parent-of-origin-resolved Granny Smith genome shows that matched references reveal sun-exposure and cold-storage responses missed by others. A Capsicum super-pangenome from 48 genomes links pungency and aroma terpene traits to Pun1 haplotypes and TPS genes. What is new is the use of haplotype-resolved and pangenome frameworks to resolve allele-specific and reference-dependent variation.

ranked.headline: DNA language models are specialized, probed, and applied to regulatory design
ranked.summary: Sequence foundation models are moving from generic pretraining toward specialized inputs, diagnostic evaluation, and enhancer design.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the adaptation of DNA sequence foundation models to narrower biological inputs and tasks. An apicomplexan-specific model pretrained on 455 assemblies improves regulatory signal prediction in data-sparse small genomes of Plasmodium falciparum, while ModBERT incorporates population variants and long-read CpG methylation to predict chromatin features and variant effects. Other preprints test what these models actually learn: LAMP examines why fine-tuning on personal genomes does not improve gene expression prediction, and fine-tuned Borzoi and AlphaGenome perform comparably to variant-based methods for whole-blood expression in admixed Latino individuals. On the design side, GENECraft couples a genomic language model with a functional oracle without training, and REGAL uses reinforcement learning over regulatory grammar to generate tissue-specific enhancers validated across species. What is new is the shift from generic pretraining toward specialized inputs, diagnostic evaluation, and constrained regulatory design.

ranked.headline: Signaling and tissue architecture organize neural progenitors during early brain development
ranked.summary: Recent preprints dissect progenitor maintenance, rosette formation and ventricular integrity using organoid, mouse and imaging approaches.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is how signaling and epithelial architecture organize neural progenitors during early brain development. A SOX9-high radial glia program is reported to couple progenitor maintenance to neuronal identity, with regulation by Notch and SOX9. Conditional loss of the Notch effector Rbpj in mice disrupts ventricular zone integrity and polarity, obstructing CSF flow and causing neonatal hydrocephalus. In human cortical organoids, neural rosettes are shown to arise from an interconnected tubular network formed through neuroepithelial folding and internalization. A whole-mount 3D imaging and quantitative platform for dorsal forebrain spheroids detects altered growth and rosette phenotypes in an isogenic Down syndrome model. The zebrafish meninges study, implicating Foxc1 and Wnt, is adjacent to this thread rather than centered on progenitor organization. What is new is the convergence of quantitative 3D tissue-scale analysis with defined regulatory programs.

ranked.headline: Lability and drift shape trait and lineage diversification across diverse taxa
ranked.summary: Five new studies link trait lability, gene flow and demographic context to uneven phenotypic and lineage diversification.
ranked.synthesis: The items converge on the view that phenotypic and lineage diversification is uneven and context-dependent rather than governed by a single uniform process. In Mimosa, diversification rates form a continuum, with radiations accounting for most diversity and disparity and linked to abiotic niche lability. In island kingfishers, faster plumage color evolution tracks faster diversification and accelerates as genomic diversity declines, implicating drift. Bark anoles show convergent signaling traits decoupled from genomic species boundaries, with gene flow shaping speciation outcomes. An analysis of 25,432 iridescent patches from 3,151 bird species finds that both Darwinian and Wallacean hypotheses explain sexual dichromatism, and sexual dimorphism in leaf-footed bugs is labile, often arising already dimorphic in new traits. The items do not share one mechanism; the common thread is the lability of traits under varying demographic and ecological context.

ranked.headline: Stress drives selective autophagy and adaptor-mediated remodeling of organelle contacts
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications assign specific adaptors, tethers and condensates to distinct stress contexts in organelle quality control.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on stress-responsive remodeling of organelles through selective autophagy, although they span different compartments and stress types. In preprints, Contact-phagy uses SIGMAR1-CCPG1 to turn over ER-mitochondria contact-site subdomains, and the yeast ER-vacuole tether Mdm1 supports starvation-induced autophagy by balancing phospholipid and neutral lipid metabolism to allow autophagosome completion. Published work links iron deficiency to pexophagy through a GABARAP-FLCN/FNIP1 interaction that activates TFEB and TFE3. Processing bodies form during recovery from lysosomal damage and collaborate with stress granules to support lysosomal quality and cell survival. RAB11 and RAB30 cooperate on endosomes under starvation, shear and osmotic stress, using phosphoinositide turnover to drive autophagy. What is new is the assignment of specific adaptors, tethers and condensates to each stress context.

ranked.headline: Nuclear RNA maturation depends on timing, composition and phase behavior
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a new abscission study link RNA maturation timing and composition to phase behavior and cell-cycle control.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that nuclear RNA maturation is defined by timing and molecular composition. In Drosophila spermatocytes, Y-loop A co-transcriptional splicing takes place within chromatin hubs, with delays that vary by transcription cluster and increase as spermatocytes mature. In yeast, nuclear mRNPs share a minimal Yra1p/Pab1p core, while most factors associate transiently in stage-specific modules shaped by intron class and promoter. Splicing also intersects with cell-cycle control, as SF3b1 relocalizes to abscission checkpoint bodies and timely abscission depends on splicing. What is new is direct perturbation and fractionation-based readouts: the covalent glue HL-1B stabilizes TOE1 on the spliceosome, altering snRNA 3'-processing and splicing in human cells, while zebrafish fractionation RNA-seq links RNA insolubility to ribosome, poly(A) tail and m6A features. The zebrafish study addresses RNA phase behavior more than splicing, so the shared thread is strongest for timing and composition rather than a unified mechanism.

ranked.headline: Designed binders and molecular glue degraders enable selective interface modulation
ranked.summary: Computational and structure-guided methods now design binders and glue degraders with defined selectivity, moving beyond empirical discovery.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is rational engineering of protein-protein interfaces and ligand-dependent modulation. Two preprints address molecular glue degraders: TrIP-MGRD targets transient PPI pockets, supported by a CDK12-DDB1 cryo-EM structure and the molecular glue C432 that stabilizes it, while an antibody-drug conjugate of a CCNK glue degrader achieves HER2-selective cyclin K degradation with antiproliferative effects in breast cancer. Computational design appears in a shared latent-space method for affinity-guided PDZ-binding peptides, including off-target-aware and dual-target design, and in MobGen, which de novo designs monobody binders against the SARS-CoV-2 Spike RBD. A paired deep mutational scanning study of full-length Lck maps activity and inhibitor sensitivity, enabling a nilotinib-sensitized variant. The new element is a shift from empirical discovery toward designed, selective, interface-aware modulation, although this pattern does not apply uniformly across all items.

ranked.headline: Methods recover shared latent structure from heterogeneous neural recordings
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply tensor, latent-variable and digital twin models to align heterogeneous neural data across sessions, subjects and recording formats.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread in these preprints is the extraction of shared latent structure from neural data that differ in session, subject or recording format. Neuralign jointly aligns and decomposes heterogeneous recordings into shared tensor components, while Unified CEBRA pools recordings across sessions through a shared label to relate single-neuron contributions to population codes in mouse visual cortex. C3PO operates directly on unsorted, unbinned continuous-time spike trains, learning predictive and interpretable latent variables. A digital twin of freely moving mouse V1 links classical tuning and behavioral gain effects to a general visual code. In Drosophila, heterogeneous short-term plasticity across Kenyon cell inputs is reported to reformat temporal information into an explicit population clock. The items do not address identical questions; the shared emphasis is on recovering interpretable latent variables while treating heterogeneity as part of the structure to be modeled.

ranked.headline: Multimodal models link mutational processes and variant effects at sequence resolution
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple mutational signature inference, sequence-based mutation prediction and variant assessment across cancer and normal tissue.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the joint modelling of mutation-generating processes and variant consequences at sequence resolution. MOTET jointly infers multimodal mutational processes across SBS, DBS and indel signatures in 2,583 PCAWG cancer genomes. A monoallelic MUTYH carrier shows the oxidative SBS18 signature across multiple normal human tissues, suggesting a single hypomorphic allele. EAGLE-MUT, a DNA language model trained on cancer mutation data, predicts somatic mutation probabilities that vary with sequence context and nucleosome positioning. Two further preprints apply computational assessment to variant interpretation: base-editing accessibility of chromosome 21 ClinVar pathogenic variants with an African-ancestry focus, and integrated AlphaFold 3, stability and AlphaGenome analysis of TP63-IRF6-GRHL3 coding and non-coding variants. What is new is the combination of multiple mutation classes and predictive sequence models with variant-level assessment, although the items differ in scope and maturity.

ranked.headline: Diffusion and functional MRI methods refine probabilistic brain connectivity estimates
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test denoising, harmonization, fusion and decomposition methods on large, incomplete or reconstructed neuroimaging datasets.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is methodological: these preprints aim to make diffusion and functional MRI connectivity estimates more reliable under noise, reconstruction, missing modalities or pooling across cohorts. One study decomposes precisely aligned HCP probabilistic tractography connectomes with non-negative matrix factorization into white matter tracts and gray matter territories. Another reports that Marcenko-Pastur denoising of diffusion MRI weakens under common image reconstruction, and that a noise covariance estimated from reconstructed images restores it. StaGIC jointly infers regional circuit heterogeneity and structural connectivity from resting-state functional data. ProgMF fuses incomplete multimodal neuroimaging data and recovers sources linked to Alzheimer's diagnosis, cognition and amyloid PET. A deep learning harmonization study preserves tinnitus-related connectivity patterns when resting-state fMRI from patients and controls is pooled. The common advance is preserving biologically meaningful connectivity structure through each processing step.

ranked.headline: tRNA supply and ribosome state shape translational control across biological systems
ranked.summary: Recent studies link tRNA pools, ribosome composition and nutrient-dependent ribosome pausing to translation regulation beyond transcript abundance.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that translational output is shaped by tRNA supply and ribosome state, not transcript abundance alone. Single-cell tRNA sequencing (sctRNA-seq) jointly profiles mRNA and tRNA abundance, linking tRNA-dependent control to cell identity. In beta-cells, high glucose reduces RPLP1 on translating ribosomes, impairing insulin translation and secretion. MYC promotes pre-tRNA maturation to expand the mature tRNA pool during re-entry into proliferation in HepaRG cells. In budding yeast, nutrient repletion engages sequence-dependent ribosome pausing and tRNA charging changes. A labelled protein ratio normalization for nascent proteome SILAC data preserves global translation changes masked by median normalization, revealing distinct targets of eIF4A1/2 and of their inhibitor silvestrol. Together, these studies position translation as a dynamically reprogrammed control layer.

ranked.headline: Individual loss and parasite pressure reshape host networks and spatial dynamics
ranked.summary: Preprints and a theoretical model converge on how network topology and spatial structure govern ecological responses to individual-level change.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is that network or spatial structure determines how individual-level changes propagate to population and community outcomes. A simulation study across 268 empirical animal social networks reports that compensatory tie formation alters how individual loss reorganises social structure, so predicted effects of losing an individual depend on whether remaining animals rewire. Two spatial studies link topology to infection and herbivory: host-parasite coevolution on spatial networks shows that degree heterogeneity drives host resistance and spatial variation in parasite infectivity, while an individual-based herbivore model shows that movement and landscape structure jointly shape resource depletion and population dynamics. A theoretical model adds that parasite-impaired host mobility reduces virulence through altered relatedness and host density, with feedbacks on prevalence. What is new is the explicit coupling of movement or tie dynamics to evolutionary and demographic outcomes, although these items are largely simulation- or theory-based.

ranked.headline: Sound exposure and hearing alter behaviour and sensitivity in aquatic animals
ranked.summary: Recent work contrasts sound effects on zebrafish and Oikopleura dioica with seasonal hearing shifts in Arctic cod.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how sound exposure and auditory sensitivity vary within aquatic species, with the source of variation differing across studies. In zebrafish, emergence latency differed among individuals and decreased across two tests, and sound exposure reduced vertical midline crossings more than ambient sound did. In Oikopleura dioica, anthropogenic noise changed behaviour in a manner dependent on life stage and signal type, with larvae appearing most sensitive. In Arctic cod, auditory evoked potential measurements revealed seasonal differences in hearing sensitivity between spawning and non-spawning fish. What is new is the explicit treatment of intra-specific variation: individual, life-stage and seasonal differences each feature in these responses to sound, rather than a single fixed response. The Arctic cod study is the only published item here, while the zebrafish and Oikopleura work are preprints and should be treated as provisional.

ranked.headline: Pregnancy estradiol signaling remodels maternal gut via regulatory T cells
ranked.summary: Recent preprints connect pregnancy and lactation to maternal tissue remodeling and to maternal immune cell transfer to neonates.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that reproductive physiology reshapes maternal tissues and their immune compartments. In a mouse preprint, pregnancy-driven estradiol signaling expands intestinal regulatory T cells that secrete IL-10 and promote stem cell proliferation, remodeling the small intestine. A separate foster-nursing mouse study reports that maternal immune cells survive neonatal gut transit, enter circulation, and reach organs and injury sites in offspring, suggesting a route of systemic transfer during breastfeeding. A single-cell and spatial transcriptomic study of dairy goat mammary tissue across dry and peak lactation describes period-specific changes in epithelial, stromal and immune populations. The items differ in species, tissue and question; the goat study is descriptive profiling, and the transfer study concerns offspring rather than maternal remodeling. What is new is the joint attention to hormonal control of intestinal immune-epithelial remodeling, maternal-to-neonatal cell transfer, and lactation-stage mammary profiling.
